nodes.name: Hydrothermal Co precursor growth
nodes.procedure: Cobalt precursors are hydrothermally grown on Ti foil. During this step, the structures of the cobalt precursors can be adjusted to be nanoneedles, nanobelts and nanorhombuses by controlling the parameters of the process such as the reaction temperature, the amount of reactants, and the usage of NH4F.
nodes.source_text: First, cobalt precursors are hydrothermally grown on Ti foil... by controlling the parameters of the process.

nodes.name: Sulfurization via Kirkendall reaction
nodes.procedure: Porous Co9S8 materials with similar morphologies are fabricated by reacting Na2S with cobalt precursors. The formation of pores in the Co9S8 products is attributed to the Kirkendall effect during sulfurization.
nodes.source_text: Second, porous Co9S8 materials... Kirkendall effect during sulfurization.

nodes.name: WS2 nanosheets hybridization
nodes.procedure: WS2 nanosheets can be in situ grown on the surface of the Co9S8 to form Co9S8/WS2 composites with nanoneedle, nanobelt and nanorhombus arrays.
nodes.source_text: Finally, WS2 nanosheets can be in situ grown on the surface of the Co9S8...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns assigned to cubic Co9S8 (JCPDS 86-2273) for sulfurized products. After WS2 hybridization, composites show both Co9S8 and WS2 phases with low intensity WS2 peaks due to quasi-amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of the products with different morphologies on Ti foil after sulfurization treatment are assigned to cubic Co9S8 (JCPDS card no. 86-2273) (Fig. S1 in the ESI†). After hybridization with WS2, the XRD patterns demonstrate that the composites are composed of Co9S8 and WS2 (Fig. S2 in the ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM reveals Ti foil fully covered by Co9S8@WS2 nanobelts growing perpendicularly with 10 μm film thickness, 10 nm thickness, 100 nm width, and 300-1000 nm gaps.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FESEM images (Fig. 1a and b) reveal that the Ti foil is fully covered by Co9S8@WS2 nanobelts... The cross-sectional SEM image in the inset of Fig. 1a shows that the nanobelts almost grow perpendicularly to the substrate and construct a film with a thickness of about 10 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanobelts composed of micropores from Kirkendall reaction. WS2 nanosheets with several layer thickness grown on Co9S8 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images in Fig. 1d and e show that the nanobelt is composed of numerous micropores derived from the Kirkendall reaction... The HRTEM image also indicates that WS2 nanosheets with several layer thickness were grown intimately on the surface of Co9S8 (Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals WS2 (002) planes with 0.643 nm spacing and Co9S8 (220) planes with 0.353 nm spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resolved lattice fringes of WS2 (002) planes with an interplanar spacing of 0.643 nm and Co9S8 (220) planes with an interplanar spacing of 0.353 nm were clearly revealed.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis indicates homogeneous distribution of Co, W, and S elements along nanobelts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping indicated a homogenous distribution of Co, W, and S elements along the nanobelts (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms show specific surface area of 78.9 m²/g for Co9S8/WS2 nanobelt array, substantially increased compared to bare Co9S8.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area of the Co9S8/WS2 nanobelt array is determined using N2 adsorption–desorption isotherms and found to be 78.9 m² g⁻¹, which is a substantially increased value compared to that of bare Co9S8 (Fig. S6 and Table S2 in the ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms chemical states of Co, S, and W elements in Co9S8/WS2 composites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical states of Co, S, and W elements in the Co9S8/WS2 composites were further confirmed via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis (Fig. S4 and Table S1 in the ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis confirms chemical composition of Co9S8/WS2 composites (Table S1 in ESI).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical states of Co, S, and W elements in the Co9S8/WS2 composites were further confirmed via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis (Fig. S4 and Table S1 in the ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in 0.04-0.14 V vs RHE range determines double layer capacitance Cdl values: 65.2 mF cm⁻² (nanobelt), 46.1 mF cm⁻² (nanoneedle), 33.5 mF cm⁻² (nanorhombus arrays), indicating ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The capacitances of Co9S8/WS2 nanobelt, nanoneedle and nanorhombus arrays are calculated to be 65.2, 46.1, and 33.5 mF cm⁻²... The measured capacitive currents are plotted as a function of scan rate and shown in Fig. 3d.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Co9S8/WS2 nanobelt array has much lower impedance than other morphologies, accelerating HER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EIS measurements indicate that the Co9S8/WS2 nanobelt array shows a much lower impedance and thus markedly accelerate HER kinetics (Fig. S18 in the ESI†).
